principles: Live executable facts outrank stale planning prose.
Host handoff should be helpful by default and hard-block only when false certainty would mislead the user.
Memory and learning hints are advisory context, not gate evidence.
Supersession must be machine-readable and human-readable.
drivers: Prevent hosts from asking users to redo completed work.
Keep implementation incremental so future stories can validate behavior before hard gates.
Make stale plan detection reusable for Codex, Claude Code, Antigravity, and future hosts.

options.name: A: Advisory truth-first preflight plus machine-readable supersession metadata
pros: Low risk for a documentation execution plan.
Lets hosts see current facts before asserting missing work.
Can be implemented incrementally across handoff, docs, and memory surfaces.
cons: Advisory mode can still be ignored until follow-up code wires it into host entrypoints.
Requires follow-up stories to turn policy into runtime behavior.

options.name: B: Immediate hard gate for every host handoff when stale documents are detected
pros: Strongest protection against repeated false tasking.
Forces hosts to inspect current facts before proceeding.
cons: Too broad for this document-only story.
Could block legitimate planning work when documents are intentionally historical or superseded.
Needs runtime implementation and careful false-positive handling.

options.name: C: Documentation note only
pros: No CLI or metadata design needed.
cons: Future hosts can miss the note exactly as they missed the outcome record.
Does not produce a reusable machine-readable contract.

chosen: A: Advisory truth-first preflight plus machine-readable supersession metadata
rationale: Choose advisory preflight plus metadata because this story is scoped to an execution plan, not runtime code. It gives a concrete implementation path while avoiding premature hard blocks. The plan can require follow-up stories to add supersession metadata, handoff preflight packs, dev-memory injection, and stale-plan warnings with tests before any hard gate is considered.

preMortem.scenario: The plan only adds prose and future hosts still miss it.
preMortem.trigger: No follow-up story wires dev_memory_preflight or supersession detection into host handoff.
preMortem.consequence: Claude/Codex/Antigravity can still tell the user stale work is undone.
preMortem.mitigation: The execution plan must define concrete implementation stories with command outputs and acceptance gates, not just recommendations.

preMortem.scenario: Supersession metadata is too vague to distinguish historical plans from active work.
preMortem.trigger: Documents say completed but lack completedByStory, completionCommit, supersededBy, or status fields.
preMortem.consequence: Host warnings become noisy and users stop trusting them.
preMortem.mitigation: Require a minimal schema and fixtures for active, completed, superseded, and historical-reference documents.

preMortem.scenario: Memory preflight is treated as authoritative gate evidence.
preMortem.trigger: A host or future gate consumes dev-memory as proof instead of advisory context.
preMortem.consequence: Non-authoritative lessons could incorrectly satisfy completion or review gates.
preMortem.mitigation: Plan must preserve dev-memory as non-authoritative and require live facts or validation for claims about completion.
